name: Liposomal amphotericin B
executiveSummary: Liposomal formulation (AmBisome-like). Usual adult/pediatric **3–5 mg/kg/day IV**; empiric/candidemia **3 mg/kg**; mucormycosis **5–10 mg/kg**. Less nephrotoxic than deoxycholate.
indications:
## Indications

- Invasive mycoses (candida, aspergillus, cryptococcus, mucorales, visceral leishmaniasis, etc.).
- Empiric therapy in persistent febrile neutropenia.
- When deoxycholate toxicity or failure occurs.

## Precautions

- Still may cause nephrotoxicity and hypokalemia — monitor.
- **Do not interchange mg/kg 1:1 with deoxycholate**.
- Infusion reactions possible (less frequent).

> Dilute only per the liposomal product label.

adulto.dose: Candidemia / empiric: **3 mg/kg/day**. Aspergillosis / severe: **3–5 mg/kg/day**. Mucormycosis: **5–10 mg/kg/day**. Visceral leishmaniasis: 3 mg/kg on specific days per guideline.
adulto.administration: Reconstitute and filter per label; dilute in 5% dextrose; infuse ~**30–60 min** (or per label). Many brands: no NS for initial reconstitution.
adulto.notes: Light protection per manufacturer. Do not mix with other drugs.

pediatrico.dose: **3–5 mg/kg/day** (older card max **250 mg/day** — now titrate by mg/kg in severe disease). Empiric/candidemia: **3 mg/kg/day**. Mucormycosis: **5–10 mg/kg/day**.
pediatrico.notes: Dose by weight. Preferred over deoxycholate in pediatrics.

neonatal.dose: Invasive candidiasis: often **3–5 mg/kg/day** under ID/NNU.

stability:
## Stability

- After reconstitution/dilution: short windows (hours) — check brand label.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, ↑ creatinine (less than conventional), fever/chills, nausea, anemia, hepatotoxicity.
